framework.summary: Large frontier developers that give privileged access to a model must keep a written security program to stop that access raising catastrophic risk, and run risk-based post-deployment monitoring.
framework.quote: shall establish, implement, and maintain a written security program reasonably designed to prevent such access from materially increasing catastrophic risk

transparency_report.summary: Large frontier developers' transparency reports must also summarize independent safety evaluation findings, limitations and identified catastrophic risks.
transparency_report.quote: a summary of the material findings, limitations, uncertainties,

incident_reporting.summary: Large frontier developers must report a significant safety incident to the state office as soon as practicable and within seven days of learning of it.
incident_reporting.quote: A large frontier developer shall report a significant safety

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: The bill sets no imminent-risk window of its own; it only refers to existing critical incident reporting.

third_party_audit.summary: Large frontier developers must have an accredited independent safety evaluator test a frontier model before first deploying it in New York and again after material changes.
third_party_audit.quote: conduct a technical evaluation of such model's capabilities, safeguards,

whistleblower.summary: Large frontier developers may not retaliate against employees or contractors who disclose violations, safety incidents or catastrophic risks.
whistleblower.quote: No large frontier developer, or contractor or subcontractor thereof, shall discharge, demote, suspend, threaten, harass, discriminate, or otherwise retaliate against an employee or contractor

registration.summary: Developers need no registration or licence; the office only accredits independent evaluators.

shutdown.summary: Developers must be able to promptly suspend or revoke privileged model access, but no model shutdown is required; the state office may temporarily restrict a risky capability or deployment on written findings.

compute_threshold.summary: The bill sets no compute threshold of its own.

revenue_threshold.summary: The bill sets no revenue coverage threshold; revenue is used only to size penalties.

harm_threshold.summary: The bill sets no harm figures of its own.

penalties.summary: The Attorney General may seek civil penalties up to one-half of one percent of annual gross revenue for knowing concealment, and up to one percent for willful concealment of critical incidents.
